For the Informant : Mr. Kaushik Sarkhel, Advocate : Mr. Abhishek Singh, Advocate ------
Order No.06 Dated- 19.09.2023 Heard the parties.

Apprehending his arrest, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail in connection with Argora P.S. Case No.343 of 2021 registered under sections 406/420 of the Indian Penal Code.
The Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner and the informant are partners.

It is further alleged that petitioner besides being the partner of Macintel Solutions was the director of E-world Techlife Private Limited and the petitioner was entrusted with the job of looking after the Kolkata operation of Macintel Solutions and the petitioner took illegal benefit of the entrustment and cheated the partnership firm of which the informant is a partner, by selling the stock of Macintal Solutions to E-world Techlife Private Limited on a price lower than the purchased price.
It is further alleged that the petitioner has misappropriated Rs.39,41,437/- and thereafter, the petitioner was ousted from the partnership firm on 04.09.2019.

It is further submitted that the allegations against the petitioner are all false and no part of cause of action has arisen for institution of the case within the jurisdiction of Argora Police Station, Ranchi as the entire transaction between the Macintel Solutions and E-world Techlife Private Limited took place at Kolkata and the office is also situated at Hazra Road, Kolkata.
It is then submitted that the petitioner has supplied goods worth Rs.7,61,69,651.58/- to the opposite party Praveen Kumar Pugalia vs The State Of Jharkhand ...

It is also submitted that the complaint has been lodged by the opposite party no.2 as a counter blast to the arbitration proceeding initiated by the petitioner and FIR No.369 dated 16.09.2019 wherein, final form has been submitted and against the same, an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. being CRR No. 839 of 2022 before the High Court at Calcutta is filed to compel the petitioner to withdraw the same.
It is next submitted that the dispute between the parties is at best a civil dispute and the arbitration proceeding is going on between the parties which is at an advance stage.
It is then submitted that the petitioner undertakes to cooperate with the investigation of the case.
Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Learned Addl. P.P. and the learned counsel for the informant opposes the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submits that the petitioner is not cooperating with mediation proceeding.
It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the informant that petitioner has several criminal antecedents.
Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner ought not to be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record,
it is pertinent to mention here that admittedly, the petitioner has committed all the offence in capacity of a partner of a partnership firm.
There is no allegation against the petitioner that petitioner has any intention to deceive the partners of the partnership firm at the time of entering into such partnership.
The only allegation against the petitioner is that the decision to sell the articles of the partnership firm at a particular price to company in which he was also a director.
There is no allegation that the petitioner has taken away the articles of partnership firm without paying any money,
Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that the dispute between the parties is basically a civil dispute.
Hence, I am of the opinion that it is a fit case where the above named petitioner be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Hence, in the event of his arrest or surrender within a period of six weeks from the date of this order, the petitioner shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned J.M. 1st Class, Ranchi, in connection with Argora P.S. Case No.343 of 2021 with the condition that the petitioner will cooperate with the investigation of the case and appear before the Investigating Officer as and when noticed by him and will furnish his mobile number and a copy of his Aadhar Card in the court below with the undertaking that he will not change his mobile number during the pendency of the case subject to the conditions laid down under section 438 (2) Cr.
